name: 007 ELEMENTS
kurzbeschreibung: The state-of-the-art James Bond experience exhibition at an altitude of 3,048 m features interactive stations and original film props.
beschreibung:
Overview

007 ELEMENTS is a unique cinematic installation at an altitude of 3,040 meters, embedded in the summit area of the Gaislachkogl directly above Sölden in the Ötztal. Opened on July 12, 2018, the exhibition is dedicated to the universe of James Bond and particularly the film Spectre (2015), whose memorable key scenes were shot in the winter of 2014/2015 along the Ötztaler Gletscherstraße and inside the adjacent gourmet restaurant ice Q. The European Film Academy awarded 007 ELEMENTS the title of "Treasure of European Film Culture".

History & Architecture

The building was designed by architect Johann Obermoser (Obermoser arch-omo ZT GmbH, Innsbruck), who also designed the valley and mountain stations of the Gaislachkoglbahn as well as ice Q. Exhibition design was led by Neal Callow, long-standing art director of the Bond productions (including Casino Royale, Skyfall, Spectre), and Tino Schaedler from the creative agency Optimist Inc.. The galleries are deliberately unheated: a constant 1–5 °C protects the surrounding permafrost soil. Nine thematic installations guide visitors from the secrets behind the Bond franchise to original film props, costumes, and immersive sound systems.

Visit & Getting There

The exhibition is tied to the operating hours of the Gaislachkoglbahn: in summer (approx. June–October) daily 09:00–16:30, closed on Mondays in June and September; in winter (approx. November–April) daily 09:00–16:30 (as of the 2025/26 season). Admission is via fixed time slots, with unlimited stay afterwards (recommended duration approx. 1.5–2 hours). Tickets (as of 2025/26): exhibition-only ticket from €26.00 (adults), combined ticket including return cable car ride from €64.00. By car: Inntalautobahn A12, exit Ötztal, then follow B186 for about 35 km to Sölden. By public transport: ÖBB train to Ötztal-Bahnhof station, then VVT bus (route 4194/320) to Sölden Gaislachkoglbahn (approx. 50–60 min.). From the valley station, ascent on Gaislachkoglbahn I and II takes around 30 minutes to reach 3,040 m.

Tips

Even in summer, warm winter clothing and sturdy footwear are essential – the exhibition rooms are kept at 1–5 °C year-round. Holders of the Ötztal Inside Summer Card travel free of charge on the cable car and receive discounts at the ticket desk. The gondolas are barrier-free, and the entire exhibition is wheelchair-accessible via elevators and ramps.
